(Computer ring tone chimes)

Morning briefing
Hail Outlandia
Continuance Year Twenty-One
Western agricultural output
Within approved range
European territorial compliance
Stable
Predictive detention accuracy
Ninety-eight point seven percent
Public sentiment
Grateful
Appointments
Three industrial stewards
Two military governors
One religious delegation

Move the governors
Raise the pardons
Cancel the priests
Adjusted

A sixth-grade student
From Residential Zone Eight
Has submitted a letter
Praising your leadership
Her name is Anna Vale
Would you like me
To send a personal response
Under your signature
Like I care
Sign whatever you sign

The girl remains upon the screen
Two braids tied with government blue
A gold-edged star beside her name
A careful page she thinks he knew
Four children cross the morning room
Two mine
Two Toy carried first
One asks where breakfast has been placed
One drags a coat along the floor
The shelf has held one honest line
Through uniforms and numbered years
Through maps replaced
Through names removed
Through every choice I did not make

I kept the paper flat and dry
I moved it when the rooms were searched
I told myself that keeping it
Was different from obedience
No one knew
No one asked
No one came because it stayed
A warning hidden in a book
Warns nothing
While the warned remain

Nineteen eighty-four
Red cloth
Third shelf
Page two hundred six
The envelope has yellowed
At the fold my thumb has used

He will kill you, too

You were right
Before the trucks
Before the woman in the blue silk coat
Before I placed your children
Beside mine for the photograph
You were right
When right still had
A person left to carry it
I read your sentence every year
And called the reading action
I kept my body near the door
And never touched the handle

I chose the meals
I chose the rooms
I chose the years that could be mine
I chose four children breathing
Over one dead woman’s line
I understood
That is the part
No history can soften

Correspondence sent
“Dear Anna
Your Leader personally thanks you
Your happiness is his reward.”
Signature authenticated

The machine answers for the man
The paper speaks for someone dead
The child writes into a room
Where no one living reads

(Sound of a Shredder: clink, scrape, clink)
(Sound of Paper tearing)
(Sound of Children laughing and running past the microphone)

Household movement detected
All occupants accounted for

Outlandia is secure

persona:
Michael Anthony Rose is a songwriter of rare insight and startling honesty. On his debut for Maricopa Records, he uses direct, unadorned language to explore the most profound human experiences: the gulf between who we were and who we are, the search for truth in a world of convenient fictions, and the quiet defiance of living an authentic life. His songs are less stories than they are confessions, built from the concrete details of a lived experience, where a reflection in a phone screen or the memory of a dream can trigger a lifetime of contemplation. Rose doesn't just sing about life; he holds a mirror up to it, capturing the small, resonant moments of realization that define us.

The central preoccupations of Rose's work are time and memory. His lyrics trace the lines from lost childhood potential to the stark realities of aging, questioning what we build to outlast ourselves and what we must learn to let go. He writes with a philosopher's curiosity and a diarist's intimacy, exploring the comfort of a shared lie in one song and the freedom of embracing dissonance in the next. This is music that navigates regret, loss, and mortality with a steady, empathetic gaze, always returning to the challenge of being present for the life one actually has, not the one that was planned.

Throughout his work, Rose reveals a vast emotional landscape. His voice moves from the raw vulnerability of admitting fear and bitterness to the quiet strength of asserting one’s own space and worth. He sings of intimate connection with a sensory richness and of profound disconnection with a heartbreaking clarity. His perspective is that of a seasoned witness, one who sees the innocence in younger generations without envy and accepts the limitations of his own body without surrender. He finds resilience not by ignoring the damage, but by standing within it and refusing to be diminished.

In the songs of Michael Anthony Rose, listeners will not find easy answers or false comfort. Instead, they will find a voice that speaks with clarity and courage to the complexities of a full-size life. It is an invitation to stop arguing with the truth, to witness the ordinary light of the day, and to find that being here, honestly and without shame, is more than enough.

impression.text: This track blends a lush, melancholic synth-pop texture with a cold, dystopian narrative atmosphere, opening with a futuristic spoken-word dialogue over gentle acoustic guitar strums and airy pads. The energy is subdued and reflective, carrying a steady, retro synth-driven pulse that feels both comforting and subtly ominous. The production is impeccably clean, prioritizing space and depth with heavily reverberated vocals and delicate acoustic elements that sit beautifully atop a warm, grounding bassline. A defining feature of the piece is this contrast between organic acoustic instruments and robotic, synthetic soundscapes, creating a compelling sci-fi soundtrack quality.

review.review_text: "Coda" is the most ambitious thing Rose has put to tape, a five-minute chamber requiem built around a morning briefing between a bored autocrat and the alto machine that runs his world. The genius is in the restraint: the piece keeps a cool, unhurried pulse in C minor, all low piano and celesta and space, so that when the internal voice finally admits "I chose four children breathing / over one dead woman's line," the confession lands with no cushion under it. Rose lets the domestic detail do the moral work, the two braids tied in government blue, the yellowed envelope worn soft at the fold, and the four-note motif that never quite completes until the celesta finishes it at the end. The sound design is a real accomplishment here, the shredder's clink and scrape, the children laughing past the mic, the flat verdict "Outlandia is secure," all of it earning that abrupt final silence. It asks patience and rewards it; the spoken briefing sections run a touch long before the emotional turn arrives, and this is not a hummable single but a piece to sit inside. A highlight, and proof of how far Rose is willing to reach.
